subject.title: fix: reject invalid channel account selections

question: Should OpenClaw adopt strict failure for every caller-supplied invalid, disabled, conflicting, or channel-mismatched account ID, even where existing automation may have relied on fallback to another configured account?
rationale: The implementation is deliberately changing an existing failure mode across several public outbound entry points; tests and live proof can show behavior, but they cannot determine whether the upgrade contract is the intended product policy.

options.title: Adopt strict explicit routing
options.body: Accept errors for invalid caller-supplied account IDs while retaining omitted and host-derived defaults, then refresh the merge-base proof before landing.

options.title: Preserve legacy fallback
options.body: Keep fallback behavior for existing explicit selections and redesign strict validation as an opt-in or otherwise separately approved compatibility policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict explicit routing
recommendation.body: Accept errors for invalid caller-supplied account IDs while retaining omitted and host-derived defaults, then refresh the merge-base proof before landing.

likelyOwner.reason: They assembled the affected routing implementation and can provide the most direct technical context, while the final compatibility choice remains a maintainer decision.
